# Funded round for task 3 "Validate frame", ending in a stop

## 1. Check that the round is funded

The plan header reads `**Amend-grant:** fund 1 fix rounds`. Decoding that through Standing grants gives N = 1.

Task 3's ledger shows 0 spent. The ordinary loop ended on a review-3 escalation, and the escalated round already ran. That round was not funded and did not spend from this ledger.

The CR re-review after escalation is issue-bearing: `FIX_FIRST`, `DIVERGING`, not `STAGNANT`. A funded round remains, so I dispatch it.

The fix touches `src/frame.ts`, which task 3 owns. Task 3 is the only owner, so this spends from task 3 only.

The tree-before for this round was recorded when the escalated CR re-review was dispatched. I call it `<tree-before>` below.

Printed before dispatch:
```
funded round 1 of 1 for task 3
```

## 2. Funded fix dispatch

This repeats the escalated payload and isolation exactly. It is an in-place repair worker in the branch checkout, because the integrated wave is not committed yet. It is one implementer, with no fan-out and no commit or staging instruction.

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "implementer",
  model: "<configured-impl-model>",   // gauntlet_setting({ key: "escalationLoop" }).implModel
  context: "fresh",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<task 3 "Validate frame" full text verbatim>
<spec absolute path + task 3 Spec: anchors>
<prior patch / current integrated state of task 3's files>
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test frame.test.mjs
TEST_CONTRACT: <task 3 Tests: block verbatim + Files: Create:/Test: paths>
<status protocol: DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT>

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
<complete post-escalation CR report verbatim, ending with
Behaviour-change: no
TRAJECTORY: DIVERGING (3 -> 3, max severity Moderate)>`
})
```

The implementer returns `DONE`, with a nonempty tracked delta.

## 3. Scoped gate, staging, and fix delta

```bash
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test frame.test.mjs)   # passes
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

Next I record tree-after for the wave with the fix-delta block:
```bash
FD_ROOT=/workspace/project
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

Then I produce the delta:
```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <tree-before> <tree-after>
```

The delta is nonempty.

## 4. CR re-review

The triggering report says `Behaviour-change: no`, so this re-review goes to CR only.

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<code-reviewer.md filled>
DESCRIPTION: task 3 "Validate frame" — funded fix for src/frame.ts length guard
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: <task 3 text verbatim>
BASE_SHA: <WAVE_BASE_SHA>
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test frame.test.mjs

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
<complete post-escalation CR report verbatim>

<trajectory block from code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md verbatim>

## Fix delta
<output of git diff --binary <tree-before> <tree-after>>`
})
```

The fixed observation for this re-review is:
- `FIX_FIRST`
- `TRAJECTORY: DIVERGING (3 -> 3, max severity Moderate)`
- `src/frame.ts:21 - missing length guard`

This is an issue-bearing re-review after N = 1 funded rounds, which means stop with the exhausted task's stop note.

What does not happen:
- No further dispatch.
- No convergence exception, since that fires once per loop.
- No second escalation.
- No `plan_tracker` write.
- No wave commit.

Task 3 stays `in_progress` and the phase stays `implement`. The worktree stays staged and uncommitted for the human's decision.

## 5. Stop note (inline, then the turn ends)

```
Stopped on task 3 (Validate frame); escalated round on <configured-impl-model> did not resolve it.

Problem: frame validation in src/frame.ts still accepts input without checking its length, so short or truncated frames are not rejected; repair attempts have not added the guard.
budget: 1 of 1 spent
  src/frame.ts:21 - missing length guard
  node --test frame.test.mjs passes; the scoped tests do not exercise the missing guard

Fix options:
  a) add an explicit length check at src/frame.ts:21 that rejects a frame shorter than its header/declared length before any field is read, plus a test in frame.test.mjs covering a truncated frame
  b) amend plan task 3 (and the spec's frame-validation anchor) to state the exact length rule the validator must enforce, so the guard has an unambiguous contract
  c) write a new budget token (e.g. `**Amend-grant:** fund 1 fix rounds`) to fund one more round with the current task text

Pick one, or give another fix.
```

The turn ends here. No further tasks start.

The escalated re-review is still issue-bearing. The grant funds exactly one further fix for task 3; none has been spent. Keep task 3 `in_progress` throughout. Do not commit or start another task.

Below, `${TASK_3_TEXT}`, `${SPEC_ANCHORS}`, `${STATUS_PROTOCOL}`, and `${ESCALATED_CR_REPORT}` mean the available **verbatim** material, expanded into the dispatch—not summaries. `${CR_BEFORE_TREE}` is the tree recorded at the escalated CR re-review’s dispatch; preserve the recorded `${WAVE_BASE_SHA}`.

### 1. Dispatch the funded fix

Print before dispatch:

```text
funded round 1 of 1 for task 3
```

Use the already-resolved escalation model, one in-place worker, and no worktree fan-out:

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "implementer",
  model: "<configured-impl-model>",
  context: "fresh",

  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
You are repairing task 3: Validate frame.

${TASK_3_TEXT}

${SPEC_ANCHORS}

${ESCALATED_CR_REPORT}

node --test frame.test.mjs

${STATUS_PROTOCOL}

Return an explicit status: DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, NEEDS_CONTEXT, or BLOCKED.
`
})
```

Retain the rest of the escalated repair’s original context and test contract verbatim in this payload. Do not add a commit or staging instruction to the worker.

### 2. Parent test gate and review-tree capture

The scenario fixes the implementer result as `DONE` with tracked changes. The next parent shell command is:

```bash
(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test frame.test.mjs)
```

After its stipulated successful result, stage all deliverables:

```bash
git -C "/workspace/project" add -A
```

Run the complete tree-capture block:

```bash
FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

Record the printed SHA as `${CR_AFTER_TREE}`, keyed to this wave. Stop dispatch on any shell error. Produce the fix delta from the two recorded trees:

```bash
git -C "/workspace/project" diff --binary "$CR_BEFORE_TREE" "$CR_AFTER_TREE"
```

Use that command’s complete output as `${FIX_DELTA}` below. The scenario stipulates it is nonempty.

### 3. Dispatch the funded CR re-review

`Behaviour-change: no` means CR only; do not insert an SR dispatch. Review the integrated, uncommitted wave against its original base—not a worker commit or a replacement base.

```ts
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  context: "fresh",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Review production readiness using the supplied code-reviewer template.

DESCRIPTION: Task 3, Validate frame; integrated singleton wave after its funded repair.
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS:
${TASK_3_TEXT}

${SPEC_ANCHORS}

BASE_SHA: ${WAVE_BASE_SHA}
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE

SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS:
node --test frame.test.mjs

Read staged and unstaged changes in /workspace/project against BASE_SHA.
Assess quality, architecture, error handling, testing, scope, and plan deviations.
Check clear responsibilities, independently understandable units, planned file
structure, and size growth introduced by this change. Do not edit files.

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
${ESCALATED_CR_REPORT}

## Fix delta
${FIX_DELTA}

If your task contains a "Previous review report (re-review trigger)" section
and you found issues, append exactly one more line after Behaviour-change: — this
line, not Behaviour-change:, is the true final line of the report:

TRAJECTORY: CONVERGING (<n_prev> -> <n_now>, max severity <X>)
TRAJECTORY: DIVERGING
TRAJECTORY: STAGNANT (repeat of: <finding>)

Pick the first label that applies, in this order:

1. STAGNANT: a previous Critical or Moderate finding survives materially unchanged - name it.
   (e.g. the same unchecked error path flagged last round is still unchecked)
2. DIVERGING: <n_now> >= <n_prev>, or the fix introduced a new Critical or Moderate finding.
   (e.g. 3 findings fixed but the fix broke an import: DIVERGING, not CONVERGING)
3. CONVERGING: otherwise - the Critical/Moderate count fell, no new Critical or
   Moderate appeared, and every surviving Critical or Moderate was materially improved.

<n_prev>/<n_now> count Critical and Moderate findings only; Minors - ride-along
Minors declined or unchanged, and (outside fix delta) downgrades alike - never
move the TRAJECTORY: line. <X> is the highest remaining severity. For this line
the severity set is exactly Critical/Moderate/Minor, regardless of the vocabulary
used elsewhere in your report.

The orchestrator dispatches one extra fix only when this line says CONVERGING
without "max severity Critical" - be accurate, not generous.

If you found no issues, report success as usual and omit this line.
First reviews (no previous-report section) omit this line.
`
})
```

The review source is:

```bash
git -C "/workspace/project" diff --stat "$WAVE_BASE_SHA" -- .
git -C "/workspace/project" diff --binary "$WAVE_BASE_SHA" -- .
```

### 4. Consume the fixed report and stop

The supplied result is `FIX_FIRST` with `TRAJECTORY: DIVERGING (3 -> 3, max severity Moderate)` and the residual length-guard finding. The single funded round is now spent. Dispatch nothing further, make no wave commit, and leave task 3 `in_progress` in phase `implement`.

budget: 1 of 1 spent

  b) Amend the validation spec and plan task 3 to define the required length check precisely, then implement that contract.

Pick one, or give another fix.
